episodes.174054: A warm front moved north across Massachusetts during the day and evening. Then a cold front approached overnight.  The result was up to 1.5 inches of rain and some localized street flooding in northeast Massachusetts.
episodes.174303: A powerful low pressure system deepening over northern Lake Huron produced storm force north winds over central and eastern Lake Superior from the 17th into the 18th.
episodes.174326: Storm force north winds developed at Minneapolis Shoal Light on the 18th in the wake of powerful low pressure center over northern Lake Huron.
episodes.174592: A lake-aggregate surface trough resided over the Great Lakes and vicinity during the evening of the 17th through wee hours of the 18th. This trough resulted from the expansion of relatively-warm lake-modified air as a cold air mass crossed the relatively-warm lakes and was warmed and moistened from beneath. An embedded and occluded surface low meandered over Lake Huron. During the late evening of the 17th through early morning of the 18th, a cyclonically-curved west-northwesterly mean low-level flow of cold air over and downwind of Lake Erie and appreciable lake-induced CAPE triggered multiple bands of lake-effect rain and graupel that targeted much of northeast OH and northwest PA. A stronger updraft associated with one of the heavier lake-effect showers managed to produce hail up to penny-size in the Painesville area in Lake County, OH.
episodes.174649: Ample moisture in advance of a cold front shifting through the region during the night led to thunderstorms capable of producing damaging wind gusts across coastal waters.
episodes.175104: Scattered severe thunderstorms associated with a cold front produced large hail across portions of central and southeast Virginia.
episodes.175108: A convective cluster moved into the interior sections of central Maine on the evening of the 17th. Another round of moderate to heavy rain aligned over the Kennebec River from Skowhegan to Gardiner. A recent soaking rain event on October 14th had saturated the ground and reduced storage in area ditches and local reservoirs ahead of the storm events on the 17th and 18th. Also compounding the flooding was leaf debris which blocked drainage and culverts.
episodes.175118: Isolated severe thunderstorm associated with a cold front produced damaging winds across portions of the Lower Maryland Eastern Shore.
episodes.175119: Scattered thunderstorms associated with a cold front produced gusty winds across portions of the York River.
episodes.175120: Scattered thunderstorms associated with a cold front produced gusty winds across portions of the Maryland Coastal Waters.

Numerous local roads were flooded as ditches and storm drains were overwhelmed with 2 to 3 inches of rainfall.
